text:
maria: Quick question — trying to configure the JS SDK to talk to a customer VPC private endpoint behind a corporate proxy. When I set baseUrl to https://internal-redwood.example and also set HTTP_PROXY, streaming generation stalls after the first chunk. Anyone seen this?
chris: Hmm, we hit similar with Node fetch + proxies. What SDK version and node runtime?
maria: SDK v2.5.1, Node 18.12. Response starts then stops — no error, just hangs until socket times out. Non-streaming requests (sync generation) work fine through the proxy.
chris: Streaming + proxy often breaks because the SDK uses chunked responses with keep-alive. Some proxies buffer until connection close. Is the corp proxy doing TLS interception or HTTP/1.0 reformatting?
maria: IT says it's doing TLS MITM with a corporate root cert. We added their cert to system store. Also tried running with env NO_PROXY for the internal host — but we need to go through proxy for auth handshake because the control plane is outside the VPC. So we must proxy initial auth, then direct to private endpoint.
devex-bot: Docs: https://redwood.example/docs/private-endpoints#proxies — recommends websocket tunnel or http CONNECT for streaming when proxy buffers.
sophie: For Node specifically: using undici as transport helps if the proxy supports CONNECT. Workaround we shipped: open a CONNECT tunnel to the target host, then use plain HTTP/1.1 over that tunnel so chunked streaming flows. Example (simplified):
```js
const { Agent } = require('undici');
const agent = new Agent({ connect: { proxy: { origin: process.env.HTTP_PROXY } } });
fetch(url, { agent, headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}` } });
```
sophie: If the proxy rewrites to HTTP/1.0 you'll still be stuck.
chris: Another option: split auth+initial setup = proxied fetch to control plane, then exchange for an ephemeral direct URL (signed private endpoint URL) and connect directly (set NO_PROXY for that host). Do you have that flow?
maria: We don't currently have signed ephemeral URLs. Customer prefers long-lived private endpoint.
sophie: Then propose one of two approaches: 1) request proxy enable CONNECT or websocket passthrough for that destination; 2) implement SDK support to optionally open an explicit CONNECT tunnel before streaming. The latter is a small change in transport layer.
ryan: Agree — add SDK flag like "tunnelProxyForStreaming": true that triggers CONNECT. We'll need tests and a feature flag for safety. Also document TLS cert pinning steps for customers that MITM.
maria: If we add tunnelProxyForStreaming, can it be toggled per-request? Some customers will want toggle per-route.
chris: Yes, make it per-request and per-client config. Default off.
devex-bot: Added docs stub: https://redwood.example/internal/devex/proxy-tunnel-ops (private).
maria: One last thing — when using a custom baseUrl with path suffix (e.g., https://internal-redwood.example/api/v1), streaming fails unless you strip trailing path and pass full path in request. Is that expected?
sophie: That was a bug we fixed in runtime v1.8.4 — path concatenation double-escapes leading slash when using undici agent + CONNECT. If you're on runtime <1.8.4, upgrade. Otherwise SDK will normalize baseUrl now.
maria: I'm on runtime 1.8.2 — upgrading now. If that doesn't fix hangs I'll open a support ticket and include packet captures.
ryan: If you include a pcap, redact customer data. Also include SDK logs with DEBUG=redwood:transport.
maria: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
chris: pinging @sophie for a PR to add "tunnelProxyForStreaming" feature toggle to the JS SDK and a short README snippet for corp proxies.
sophie: On it — will open RFC and draft tests.
maria: Appreciate it, team.
